RESULT: both CI numbers reproduce exactly, and every unmatched entry is classified. Method: origin/main 53970b80, release build, scratch scripts in the worktree (scratch/, uncommitted) importing scripts/weekly.py, corpora under agent-a9b8's .corpora (read-only). Not checked: I did not download weekly.json from run 41479003541; the "reproduces" claim rests on the CI percentages you gave me.

REPRODUCTION
- shadcn: rdt_with_props 1594, excluded 21 (lib_members 11, promise_props 5, not_jsx 4, hook 1), exact 1518, paired 0, reference 1573, recall 1518/1573 = 96.5%. Unmatched: 55.
- antd: rdt_with_props 258, excluded 43, exact 165, paired 8 (default_export 6, named_export 2), merged 8, reference 207, recall 165/207 = 79.7%. Unmatched: 42.
- --include-unexported matters little. With exported-only Caliper, shadcn is 1517/1573 and antd 163/207. So unexported components explain at most 1 and 2 matches, and no misses. All 97 unmatched fail for other reasons.

SHADCN, 55 unmatched (apps/v4/...)
S1 object-literal members, 35 (icons.tsx 19, mdx-components.tsx 16).
 - icons.tsx:logo, twitter, github, spinner, v0. `export const Icons = { logo: (props: IconProps) => <svg/>, ... }`.
 - mdx-components.tsx:h1..h6, table, pre, code, Step, Steps, Image, Tab, Link, LinkedCard. `export const mdxComponents = { h1: ({...}: React.ComponentProps<"h1">) => ... }`.
 - Real? Yes in the sense that they are JSX-returning arrow functions. They are not documentation targets, though: Icons are internal site SVGs, and mdx members are mapping entries for MDX tags. Their 280-300 props are all React intrinsics (ComponentProps<"h1">), so they inflate prop recall too.
 - Structural? Yes. Add a rule for `const X = { key: (props: T) => JSX }` where each value is an arrow or function with a props parameter and a JSX return. It would sit in crates/core/src/extractor, in the component-discovery pass over variable declarators; I did not open the Rust code to pick the file. Name them "Icons.logo", which norm_name already reduces to the last segment.
 - Cost: 35 components that are mostly noise for Storybook. Better to count them as "object-literal members" or exclude them than to chase them.
S2 aliases of external components, 12 (all structural, but the types live in node_modules).
 - chart.tsx:tooltip and chartlegend in 4 registries, 8 entries. `const ChartTooltip = RechartsPrimitive.Tooltip` and `const ChartLegend = RechartsPrimitive.Legend`. RDT names them after recharts' own class (Tooltip, Legend).
 - combobox.tsx:comboboxroot (base, radix, new-york-v4) and select.tsx:selectroot (base): `const Combobox = ComboboxPrimitive.Root`, `const Select = SelectPrimitive.Root`, 4 entries.
 - Real? Yes. They are the public Chart/Combobox/Select roots, and shadcn's Storybook would document them.
 - Structural? Only the alias is structural; the props require resolving the imported library's types. That is the TS checker or --load-dependencies. Binding names differ from RDT's (Combobox vs ComboboxRoot), so pairing also needs an alias rule.
S3 external re-exports, 3: bases/aria/ui/combobox.tsx:collection (`Collection as ComboboxCollection`), bases/base/ui/direction.tsx:directionprovider, bases/aria/ui/direction.tsx:i18nprovider (`export { I18nProvider }` of react-aria-components). Real components; no local definition, so this would need the TS checker or dependency loading, and probably should not be counted against Caliper.
S4 call-result components, 5: registry/icons/icon-{lucide,hugeicons,phosphor,remixicon,tabler}.tsx. `export const IconLucide = createIconLoader("lucide")`, which returns `function IconLoader({name, ...}: {name: string} & ComponentProps<"svg">)`. Real? Yes, but internal registry plumbing. A structural rule is possible: a factory in the same package whose single returned function is the component. Low value.

ANTD, 42 unmatched (components/...)
A1 default export bound to a different name than RDT's, in the same file, 21. RDT names a default export after the file; Caliper names it by binding. Caliper does have the component in the same file, so this is a pairing miss in the harness, not a Caliper miss. pair() only follows default exports into another file (`target[0] != file`).
 - skeleton/Avatar.tsx:avatar (Caliper SkeletonAvatar), Button/Image/Input/Node likewise (5 total).
 - space/Addon.tsx (SpaceAddon), statistic/Number.tsx and Timer.tsx, transfer/Section.tsx (TransferSection), checkbox/Group.tsx (CheckboxGroup), radio/group.tsx (RadioGroup, `export default React.memo(RadioGroup)`).
 - menu/menu.tsx (InternalMenu), image/PreviewGroup.tsx (InternalPreviewGroup), image/Progress.tsx (Caliper ImageProgress).
 - color-picker/components/ColorSlider.tsx (SingleColorSlider), typography/Base/Ellipsis.tsx (EllipsisMeasure), tour/panelRender.tsx (TourPanel), tree/utils/iconUtil.tsx (SwitcherIconCom), table/hooks/useFilter/FilterWrapper.tsx (FilterDropdownMenuWrapper), locale/index.tsx (LocaleProvider).
 - splitter/Panel.tsx: the RDT entry is InternalPanel, which has `InternalPanel.displayName = 'Panel'`. Caliper reports 'Panel' twice, so the two collide on one key.
 - Real? Yes, all are components Caliper already reports. Fix is in weekly.py: pair a same-file default export through the local name, and treat displayName as an alias. No Caliper change.
A2 barrel index whose default export is a wrapped or cast alias, 6: collapse/index.tsx:collapse, table/index.tsx:table, radio/index.tsx:radio, statistic/index.tsx:statistic, masonry/index.tsx:masonry, dropdown/index.tsx:dropdown. Caliper reports Collapse, Table, Radio, Statistic, Masonry and Dropdown in the sibling files. The pairing chain breaks on forms the regex does not unwrap: `export default Object.assign(Collapse, {...})`, `export default ForwardTable`, `Masonry as (...)`, `const Dropdown = InternalDropdown as ...`, `Statistic as CompoundedStatistic`. Real? Yes. Harness fix only.
A3 components made by a factory function or generic call, 6: calendar/generateCalendar.tsx, calendar/index.tsx:calendar, date-picker/index.tsx:datepicker (a 382-prop DatePicker), generatePicker/index.tsx, generateRangePicker.tsx, generateSinglePicker.tsx. The component is declared inside `const generateCalendar = <D>(cfg) => { const Calendar = React.forwardRef(InternalCalendar) ... return Calendar }`, and `const Calendar = generateCalendar<Dayjs>(dayjsGenerateConfig)`. Real? Yes: Calendar, DatePicker and RangePicker are public antd components, the largest real misses. Structural? Partly. A rule for "const X = factory<...>(...), where factory is a local function that returns a forwardRef/FC defined inside it" would go in the same declarator pass; props come from the factory's inner props type with DateType generic.
A4 external symbols that antd re-exports or destructures, 3: form/Form.tsx:list (`import { List } from '@rc-component/form'`), mentions/index.tsx:option (`export const { Option } = RcMentions`), tree-select/index.tsx:treenode (`export { TreeNode }`). Real? Yes (Form.List, Mentions.Option, TreeSelect.TreeNode). Structural? Only with the checker or dependency loading; same as S2/S3.
A5 static properties assigned to components, 2: tour/index.tsx `Tour._InternalPanelDoNotUseOrYouWillBeFired = PurePanel`, and config-provider/index.tsx `ConfigProvider.config = setGlobalConfig`. Not real. The first is an internal API (PurePanel). The second is a function that takes config, not a component. A shape rule would catch both: an assignment to `X.member` whose value is not an in-file JSX-returning function; a name matching `_Internal...DoNotUse` is a secondary signal.
A6 not a component or an RDT artefact, 3: modal/confirm.tsx:confirm (`export default function confirm(config: ModalFuncProps)` returns a `{destroy, update}` handle, no JSX; rule: default export named after the file, no JSX return); tree/utils/dropIndicator.tsx:dropindicator (`dropIndicatorRender`, a render callback, not rendered as a tag); result/index.tsx:RefIcon (384 props including `default` and `form`, and no such symbol in the file; looks like an external icon type RDT attributed to the file). The first two are exclusion-rule candidates: no JSX return, or a name ending `Render`. The third has no file-level evidence.
A7 JSX hidden behind a call, 1: qr-code/QrcodeStatus.tsx:qrcodestatus. `export default function QRcodeStatus({...}: QRcodeStatusProps)` ends with `return mergedStatusRender({...})`, which is a call rather than JSX. Real but internal (used by QRCode). Caliper presumably skips it because the return is not JSX; I did not confirm that in the Rust code. A rule could accept an uppercase function whose parameter is a named props type and which builds JSX in the body.

RANKED TABLE (class, count, real component, fix)
1. A1 same-file default alias (antd): 21, yes, harness-only fix (extend pair() in weekly.py to same-file default exports and displayName). Biggest and cheapest: it alone lifts antd recall from 79.7% to about 89.9% (186/207).
2. S1 object-literal members: 35, partly (JSX functions, mostly site-internal), structural; or exclude as non-documentation. Biggest shadcn item.
3. A2 barrel cast/Object.assign alias (antd): 6, yes, harness-only fix (unwrap `as`, `Object.assign` and local `const X = Y as T`).
4. A3 factory/generic-call components: 6, yes (public DatePicker, Calendar), structural but harder (inner-component and generic factory rule).
5. S2 external aliases (Chart/Combobox/Select): 12, yes, needs dependency types; alias rule structural, props not.
6. S3 external re-exports (shadcn): 3, yes, checker or dependencies only.
7. A4 external re-exports (antd): 3, yes, checker or dependencies only.
8. S4 createIconLoader call-result: 5, yes but internal, structural but low value.
9. A5 static properties: 2, no, exclusion rule by shape.
10. A6 not components: 3, no, exclusion rule by shape (no-JSX return) or unfixable (RefIcon).
11. A7 JSX behind a call: 1, yes (internal), structural rule possible.
Shadcn totals: 35+12+3+5 = 55. Antd totals: 21+6+6+3+2+3+1 = 42.

CAVEAT: Caliper's Rust code was not read, so statements about why it skips a shape (A3, A7, S1) come from the source shape, not from its implementation. Scratch scripts are in /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/agent-a72ef5460a950f793/scratch/ (un.py lists the unmatched; outputs scratch/shadcn.txt and scratch/antd.txt). Nothing was committed.
